about: The closed lists a concept-explainer plan may use. Every label in a plan comes from here and is assigned by the classifier, never by the writer. `reads_as` is what the classifier is told to look for.

parts.name: Open
parts.job: Earn the next minute: say what this is and why to stay.

parts.name: Explain
parts.job: Make it understood: what it is, how it works, how the options differ.

parts.name: Show and build
parts.job: Make it believed: the thing running, or built step by step.

parts.name: Judge
parts.job: Say what to do with it: advice, doubts answered, when to use which.

parts.name: Series
parts.job: Place this video among its episodes. Only when the notes say it is part of a series.

parts.name: Close
parts.job: Leave something to keep: the idea landed, the ask, the goodbye.

chapter_types.name: Introduction
chapter_types.reads_as: Opens the video: a hook or a promise, a first plain statement of what the thing is, and the parts ahead.

chapter_types.name: Demo first
chapter_types.reads_as: Opens the video on the thing working before anything is explained, then says what was just seen and what will be learned.

chapter_types.name: Problem
chapter_types.reads_as: What goes wrong without it: the pain, the risk or the limit, before any answer is given.

chapter_types.name: Story
chapter_types.reads_as: How it came about, told as events in the first person: what was tried, what failed, what changed.

chapter_types.name: Concept
chapter_types.reads_as: What the thing is and why it matters. Often opens on a question and answers it with a definition and an example.

chapter_types.name: How it works
chapter_types.reads_as: A mechanism, a pipeline or an architecture walked through part by part, cause and effect.

chapter_types.name: Options compared
chapter_types.reads_as: One option or pattern among several, or two set against each other: what it is, how it handles the case, what it costs.

chapter_types.name: Worked example
chapter_types.reads_as: Sets up the one concrete case the video keeps returning to: the scenario, what it needs, why the obvious answer is not enough.

chapter_types.name: Demo
chapter_types.reads_as: The thing running: what is done, what comes back, and what that shows.

chapter_types.name: Build
chapter_types.reads_as: Steps, code or configuration, in the order they are done, each with its reason.

chapter_types.name: Feature tour
chapter_types.reads_as: What you get, one item after another: benefits, features or tricks, each with what it buys.

chapter_types.name: Advice
chapter_types.reads_as: Rules of thumb, costs, traps and when to use which, said as guidance to the viewer.

chapter_types.name: Questions
chapter_types.reads_as: A doubt or a common question the viewer would raise, stated and then answered.

chapter_types.name: Series recap or map
chapter_types.reads_as: What one earlier episode covered, what a coming episode will cover, or where this video sits in its series.

chapter_types.name: Recap
chapter_types.reads_as: The video in a few points, ending on the one line to keep.

chapter_types.name: Outro
chapter_types.reads_as: The idea landed once more, then the ask and the goodbye.

beat_types.name: Turn
beat_types.job: Give it a reason to go on.

beat_subtypes.name: Hook
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The opening grab: a question the viewer already has, a bold claim, a shared pain, a scenario. Only at the very start of the video.

beat_subtypes.name: Promise
beat_subtypes.reads_as: What the viewer will know or be able to do by the end of the video.

beat_subtypes.name: Need
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The pain, the limit or the wish that the product or the idea answers, said before the answer.

beat_subtypes.name: Announcement
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The news itself: it is out, it is new, we are introducing it.

beat_subtypes.name: Who is speaking
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A name and a greeting, or the show's name.

beat_subtypes.name: Authority
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Why this person is worth listening to on this subject.

beat_subtypes.name: Agenda
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The parts ahead, named in order.

beat_subtypes.name: Go line
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The last short line before the first part, such as: let's get started.

beat_subtypes.name: Banter
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Social talk, a joke or a reaction that carries no content.

beat_subtypes.name: Definition
beat_subtypes.reads_as: What a thing is, in plain words, and what it is for. Names or introduces the thing.

beat_subtypes.name: Analogy
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Something familiar from another world that behaves the same way.

beat_subtypes.name: Mechanism
beat_subtypes.reads_as: How it works inside, one part after another, cause and effect. Describes the thing itself, not a made-up case.

beat_subtypes.name: Worked example
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A concrete case or scenario with particulars (a customer, an order, a named request), set up or returned to, used to show the idea at work.

beat_subtypes.name: A step
beat_subtypes.reads_as: An instruction, or what is being done now, in the order it is done.

beat_subtypes.name: Code
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Code, a configuration or a screen is read out part by part, with the reason for each part.

beat_subtypes.name: A list
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Several parallel items named one after another, each with a line or two: features, benefits, parts, tools.

beat_subtypes.name: Contrast
beat_subtypes.reads_as: This, not that: two things set against each other so the difference is the point.

beat_subtypes.name: Story
beat_subtypes.reads_as: How it came about, told as events, often in the first person.

beat_subtypes.name: Proof first
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A result or a demo shown at the very start, before anything is explained.

beat_subtypes.name: Demonstration
beat_subtypes.reads_as: It is run and the result is read out.

beat_subtypes.name: What we built
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A finished result told in the first person: we built this, and here it is.

beat_subtypes.name: Evidence
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A figure, a benchmark or a study given as proof.

beat_subtypes.name: A witness
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Someone else says it: a customer, a guest, the community.

beat_subtypes.name: The question
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A question asked aloud that the following lines will answer.

beat_subtypes.name: First attempt
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The obvious or naive way of doing it, described so that the next lines can show where it falls short.

beat_subtypes.name: The turn
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The obvious answer breaks, a limit appears, or the case changes: but there is a problem. Short.

beat_subtypes.name: Objection
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A doubt the viewer might have is voiced by the speaker (you might think, but is it not) and then answered.

beat_subtypes.name: Judgment
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The speaker's own verdict or opinion on something: what they hold to be good, bad, important or overrated.

beat_subtypes.name: So-what
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The gain or the consequence of what was just explained: this means, so, that is why. It adds no new mechanism.

beat_subtypes.name: Principle
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A general rule stated as a rule, holding beyond this case. Not addressed to the viewer as a tip.

beat_subtypes.name: Signpost
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Announces what comes next or where we are: now let's look at, next, first. Carries no content of its own.

beat_subtypes.name: Naming the tool
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The product's name said once, and where to find it, when it is not news.

beat_subtypes.name: Hand-over
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Thanks to one speaker and over to the next.

beat_subtypes.name: Host's question
beat_subtypes.reads_as: One speaker asks another what the viewer would ask.

beat_subtypes.name: Community question
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A viewer's question read out.

beat_subtypes.name: Series recap
beat_subtypes.reads_as: What an earlier episode covered and where this one sits.

beat_subtypes.name: Map of the series
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The episodes or the season named one at a time, or what one coming episode will teach.

beat_subtypes.name: Milestone
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Where we have got to, in a few words, with nothing new: so now we have.

beat_subtypes.name: Bridge
beat_subtypes.reads_as: One line that closes the part just finished and opens the next: that is the what, now the how.

beat_subtypes.name: Recap
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Points already made earlier are repeated in short, for the whole video or for the part just finished. Nothing new is added.

beat_subtypes.name: Advice
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A tip, a rule of thumb, a warning or a best practice addressed to the viewer: do this, avoid that, use it when.

beat_subtypes.name: Where to get it
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Where it is available and where to start.

beat_subtypes.name: The ask
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A request to the viewer: links, comment, subscribe, try it, join.

beat_subtypes.name: Sign-off
beat_subtypes.reads_as: Thanks and goodbye.

beat_subtypes.name: Landing
beat_subtypes.reads_as: The main idea of the whole video said once more in one line, just before the asks and the goodbye, often by returning to the opening or to the carried example.

beat_subtypes.name: Look ahead
beat_subtypes.reads_as: What the next video covers.

beat_subtypes.name: A question back
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A question put to the viewer to answer for themselves or in the comments.

beat_subtypes.name: Tag
beat_subtypes.reads_as: A gag after the goodbye.

material_kinds.name: Mechanism
material_kinds.reads_as: Says how something works: parts, order, cause and effect.

material_kinds.name: Step or command
material_kinds.reads_as: Something to do, or a command, in an order.

material_kinds.name: Code or configuration
material_kinds.reads_as: Code, configuration, a schema or an API call.

material_kinds.name: List
material_kinds.reads_as: Several features, parts or options named side by side.

material_kinds.name: Difference
material_kinds.reads_as: How two things differ, or a trade-off between them.

material_kinds.name: Number or evidence
material_kinds.reads_as: A figure, a limit, a cost, a benchmark, a date.

material_kinds.name: Advice
material_kinds.reads_as: A rule of thumb, a warning, when to use which.

material_kinds.name: Background
material_kinds.reads_as: Who made it, why, how it came about.

material_kinds.name: Problem
material_kinds.reads_as: A pain, a risk or a limit that the idea answers.

material_kinds.name: Real demo
material_kinds.reads_as: A demonstration that exists and can be shown.

material_kinds.name: Availability
material_kinds.reads_as: Where to get it, links, what to read next.

material_kinds.name: Series fact
material_kinds.reads_as: What another episode of the same series covers.

routes.name: What, why, how
routes.reads_as: The notes are about one thing: what it is, why it matters, how it works or is used.

routes.name: Options
routes.reads_as: The notes hold several options, patterns or designs and how to choose among them.

routes.name: Problem, fix, proof
routes.reads_as: The notes hold a pain, the thing that fixes it and proof that it works.

routes.name: Questions
routes.reads_as: The notes are best read as a chain of questions, each answered.

routes.name: Steps
routes.reads_as: The notes are a procedure in the order it is done.

routes.name: Series
routes.reads_as: The notes are mostly about the episodes of a series: what each covered or will cover.

hooks.name: Question
hooks.reads_as: Opens on a question the viewer already has.

hooks.name: Surprising number
hooks.reads_as: Opens on a figure the viewer would not expect.

hooks.name: Counterintuitive claim
hooks.reads_as: Opens on a claim that contradicts what the viewer believes.

hooks.name: Shared pain
hooks.reads_as: Opens on a frustration the viewer knows first-hand.

hooks.name: Metaphor
hooks.reads_as: Opens on a comparison with something from another world.

hooks.name: Stakes
hooks.reads_as: Opens on what is gained or lost.

hooks.name: Promise
hooks.reads_as: Opens by saying what the viewer will know or be able to do.

hooks.name: Proof
hooks.reads_as: Opens on the thing working, or on a result.

hooks.name: No hook
hooks.reads_as: Opens on a greeting or a plain statement of the subject.

landings.name: Callback
landings.reads_as: Returns to the opening or to the carried example.

landings.name: Distillation
landings.reads_as: States the idea in one short sentence.

landings.name: Generalization
landings.reads_as: Widens the idea beyond this case.

landings.name: Invitation
landings.reads_as: Hands it to the viewer: now you build.

landings.name: No landing
landings.reads_as: Ends on the ask or the goodbye with no line that lands the idea.

presence.name: Person
presence.reads_as: The speaker talks to the viewer and nothing has to be shown: a promise, a greeting, a question, a turn, an opinion, a bridge, the ask, the goodbye.

presence.name: Person with content
presence.reads_as: The usual case when a presenter explains something that has to be seen: a diagram, a list, code or a screen is shown and the speaker stays in view beside it.

presence.name: Content
presence.reads_as: Rare with a presenter. Only when what is shown needs the whole frame or runs on its own: a full-screen recording or demo, a title card, an end card.

layouts.name: Full frame
layouts.reads_as: The person fills the frame. The promise, a turn, a judgment, the goodbye.

layouts.name: Full frame, close
layouts.reads_as: A closer framing for a change of gear inside one speech: an aside, an analogy told to camera.

layouts.name: Framed on a ground
layouts.reads_as: The person in a rounded window on the brand ground: a softer full frame.

layouts.name: Person behind a glass card
layouts.reads_as: The person fills the frame and a translucent card of a title and a few points sits over one side. A short list or an agenda said to camera.

layouts.name: Split
layouts.reads_as: The frame is halved between the person and the content. An agenda, a recap, a step, an objection answered on a diagram.

layouts.name: Panel and portrait
layouts.reads_as: The content builds in a large panel and the person stays in a tall portrait beside it. Long explanations in one layout.

layouts.name: Corner window
layouts.reads_as: The content fills the frame and the person sits in a small window in one corner. A mechanism, a worked example, code, a terminal.

layouts.name: Avatar and a speech bubble
layouts.reads_as: The person as a small cut-out with speech bubbles: a worked example read as a dialogue.

layouts.name: Graphic on a plain ground
layouts.reads_as: A diagram or an illustration that needs the whole frame, with nobody on screen.

layouts.name: Card on the ground
layouts.reads_as: One figure, one statement or one block of code set as a card on the ground.

layouts.name: Recording fills the frame
layouts.reads_as: A product screen, an editor or a terminal, edge to edge.

layouts.name: Title card
layouts.reads_as: A name on its own: the video's title, a chapter's title, the end card.

overlays.name: Name lower third
overlays.reads_as: Who is speaking. Once, for four to eight seconds.

overlays.name: A term beside the person
overlays.reads_as: A new term, the moment it is first said.

overlays.name: Stacked chips
overlays.reads_as: A short list, one chip per item as it is named.

overlays.name: A title and numbered questions
overlays.reads_as: The chapter's question, before the diagram takes over.

overlays.name: A name and a link pill
overlays.reads_as: The tool just named, and where to find it.

overlays.name: A question as a caption
overlays.reads_as: A viewer's question held on screen while it is answered.

picture_types.name: Camera only
picture_types.reads_as: The person and the set, nothing else.

picture_types.name: Camera and type
picture_types.reads_as: A few words set on or beside the person: a name, a term, a question.

picture_types.name: List
picture_types.reads_as: Bullets that build, one per phrase.

picture_types.name: Chips and cards
picture_types.reads_as: Short labels in boxes, one per item.

picture_types.name: Number card
picture_types.reads_as: One figure, large, on its own.

picture_types.name: Title or chapter card
picture_types.reads_as: A name on its own: the video, a chapter, the end.

picture_types.name: Slide
picture_types.reads_as: A heading, a few lines and a picture.

picture_types.name: Diagram
picture_types.reads_as: Boxes, arrows, a pipeline, a loop or a comparison that builds with the voice.

picture_types.name: Illustration
picture_types.reads_as: A picture drawn for this one idea: a metaphor or a scene.

picture_types.name: Typeset code
picture_types.reads_as: Code set as a card, with lines lit as they are read.

picture_types.name: Terminal or editor
picture_types.reads_as: A real session: commands, output, an editor.

picture_types.name: Product screen
picture_types.reads_as: The product's own interface in use.

picture_types.name: Document or page
picture_types.reads_as: A paper, a plan or a web page.

picture_types.name: What the product made
picture_types.reads_as: The output itself: an answer, an image, a video.

moves.name: Reveal
moves.reads_as: Something that was not on screen arrives: a box draws itself, a word types on, a card pops in, a line grows.

moves.name: Count
moves.reads_as: A value changes in place: a number counts up, a bar or a ring fills to its value.

moves.name: Emphasise
moves.reads_as: Something already on screen is pointed at without changing: a glow, a ring, an underline, a lit line of code, the rest dimming.

moves.name: Morph
moves.reads_as: Something already on screen becomes something else or moves to a new place: its state or label changes, a card grows into a panel, items regroup, a token travels along a path.

moves.name: Camera
moves.reads_as: The view itself moves: a push in on one part, a pan to the next station, a pull back to the whole.

moves.name: Carry
moves.reads_as: An object from the frame before stays on screen across the cut and becomes part of this picture.
moves.from: the product: a carrier crosses the cut

moves.name: Hold
moves.reads_as: Nothing new happens: the finished picture stays still so it can be read.
moves.from: HyperFrames: end on a still read

marks.name: Chapter title in the panel
marks.where: a chapter start, when the theme uses one

themes.name: Presenter with a corner window
themes.stage: full bleed: the set, or a white ground

themes.name: Panel and portrait
themes.stage: one ground, a panel on the left and a portrait on the right

themes.name: Framed stage
themes.stage: a coloured ground with the picture in a rounded window that never leaves

themes.name: Expert to camera
themes.stage: the set, full bleed; diagrams on a plain ground

motion_styles.name: Outline, then fill
motion_styles.reveal: an object draws its outline, then fills
motion_styles.accent: one accent colour marks the active object

motion_styles.name: Pop in order
motion_styles.reveal: chips and cards pop in, one per phrase
motion_styles.ease: one smooth ease, a small spring on chips only
motion_styles.accent: the active chip takes the accent

motion_styles.name: Type on and pop
motion_styles.accent: the brand shapes carry the joins

motion_styles.name: Carry across cuts
motion_styles.reveal: the focal object keeps developing; support arrives when it explains

relations.name: The same picture goes on
relations.reads_as: This frame keeps the picture of the frame before and adds to it.

relations.name: The next step
relations.reads_as: This frame is the next item in a sequence the frame before belongs to: the next step, the next option, the next item.

relations.name: A deeper layer
relations.reads_as: This frame shows the same thing as the frame before at another level: what is inside it, or what lies under it.

relations.name: Into a detail
relations.reads_as: This frame goes into one part of the picture before.

relations.name: A new topic
relations.reads_as: This frame starts something unrelated to the picture before.

relations.name: Person and content swap
relations.reads_as: The subject is the same; only who has the frame changes, from the person to the content or back.

arrangements.name: One thing, centred
arrangements.reads_as: One object or one statement holds the frame: a term, a figure, a single hero picture.

arrangements.name: A row
arrangements.reads_as: A few equal items side by side: three options, three cards, a short set of chips.

arrangements.name: A stack
arrangements.reads_as: Items one under another: a list, bullet rows, layers named top to bottom.

arrangements.name: A pipeline
arrangements.reads_as: Stages in a line with connectors: input, steps, output; a request passing through parts.

arrangements.name: A hub
arrangements.reads_as: One thing in the middle with others around it and lines between: an agent and its tools, a router and its specialists.

arrangements.name: A tree
arrangements.reads_as: One thing at the top with branches under it: a hierarchy, a family of variants, choices that fork.

arrangements.name: A loop
arrangements.reads_as: Stages that return to the start: a cycle that repeats.

arrangements.name: Two sides
arrangements.reads_as: Two things set against each other, left and right: before and after, this and that.

arrangements.name: Layers
arrangements.reads_as: One thing inside or on top of another: a stack of levels, a box within a box.

arrangements.name: A timeline
arrangements.reads_as: Points along a line in time order: episodes, versions, moments in a session.

arrangements.name: A grid
arrangements.reads_as: Many small equal items in rows and columns: a matrix, a wall of tiles.

arrangements.name: A code panel
arrangements.reads_as: A block of code or configuration with lines that light as they are read.
